name: tor16_fig4_fig7_network
source: YuLav16TOR pp.1166-1167, 1169 (PDF pp.4,5,7): Fig. 4(a) graph, Fig. 4(b) gadget, Fig. 5 (T=2 full network), Fig. 6 (compact), Fig. 7 (2-arc gadget)
robot_indexing: robot 0 = r1 (s1+ -> s1-), robot 1 = r2 (s2+ -> s2-)
notes: The instance drawn in Fig. 5 (T=2) is infeasible: both shortest paths have length 3 and the optimum makespan is 4, so the T=2 network only admits a multiflow of value < 2 (computed maxflow value per T is recorded).

Fig. 5/6 draw the loopback e2 (and the two 'bold blue' goal arcs of r2) at row 2 (junction A), not at row 1 (s2-); the s2- label sits between the two rows. Under Fig. 4(a)'s topology this is inconsistent.

Theorem 1 claims a bijection, but the full network lets a robot 'stay' at u by u(t)’ -> merge -> split -> u(t+1) through any incident gadget instead of the green arc; several flows map to the same path (counts recorded). The map flows->paths is surjective onto collision-free plans but not injective.
Full network per gadget: 2 internal vertices, 5 arcs (2 in, 1 middle with cost 1, 2 out). |V'| = |V|(2T+1) + 2|E|T, |E'| = 2|V|T + 5|E|T + n.
Compact (Fig. 6/7): |V'| = |V|(T+1), |E'| = |V|T + 2|E|T (+ n loopbacks); 2 variables per robot per gadget instead of 5; ratio of arcs for this graph = 32/74.
